title: 7 Best Brick Sealers in 2026: Breathable Exterior Brick Picks
metaDescription: Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500 is the best brick sealer for exterior walls and chimneys. 7 picks ranked, plus patios, coverage and how long a seal lasts.
keywords: best water seal for brick and mortar
intro:
The best brick sealer for exterior walls, chimneys and retaining walls is Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500, a breathable silane-siloxane repellent that sheds rain while letting the wall dry out. Masonry Defender and Foundation Armor SX5000 WB do the same job for less, and Siloxa-Tek 8510 adds richer color on faded brick patios.

Many brick walls never need a sealer at all. Sealing earns its place when brick takes on rain faster than it can dry: soft or old brick, walls facing the weather, chimneys, retaining walls and patios. For those jobs a breathable penetrating repellent is the right tool, and a glossy film almost never is. Below are seven picks, then the questions that decide whether and how to seal your brick.
quickAnswer: For exterior brick, choose a breathable silane-siloxane penetrating repellent such as Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500, Masonry Defender or Foundation Armor SX5000 WB. For a brick patio with faded color, Siloxa-Tek 8510. For a chimney from a home center today, DRYLOK Natural Look. Keep film-forming sealers like Seal-Krete Clear-Seal on interior brick, and fix gutters, flashing and mortar before you seal anything.

sections.heading: Best Brick Sealer for Exterior: The Short Answer
sections.body:
| Pick | Best for | Key spec |

| Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500 | Exterior walls, chimneys, retaining walls | Silane-siloxane, breathable, no sheen |
| Masonry Defender | Sealing a whole house on a budget | Water-borne silane-siloxane |
| Foundation Armor SX5000 WB | Low-odor walls and patios | Water-based silane-siloxane |
| Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8510 | Faded brick patios and garden walls | Penetrating repellent plus enhancer |
| Thompson's WaterSeal Multi-Surface | Planters, edging, small jobs | Multi-surface clear repellent |
| DRYLOK Natural Look | Chimneys, home-center availability | Breathable siloxane |
| Seal-Krete Clear-Seal | Interior brick, fireplace surrounds | Water-based acrylic film |

The single property that matters most on exterior brick is breathability. Water reaches a wall from the face, the ground, the top and from condensation inside, and the wall stays healthy by drying out through its face. A penetrating repellent keeps that path open; a film can close it and trap water where it freezes.

Penetrating repellents also leave brick looking as it did, never peel and never need stripping before the next coat, which is why they last longest in practice.

sections.heading: The 7 Best Brick Sealers in 2026, Ranked
sections.body:
The seven are ranked on paper, not on test walls: each maker's technical data sheet, the surfaces and exposures each product is rated for, the chemistry it uses and the praise and complaints that keep coming up in owner feedback. Breathable penetrating repellents take the top spots because they suit the most brick in the most climates. None of these was applied to brick of our own.

### Best Overall: Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500

Siloxa-Tek 8500 is Ghostshield's penetrating silane-siloxane repellent, and it is the product to start with for exterior brick walls, chimneys and retaining walls. The two halves of the blend split the work: small silane molecules reach deep into dense material, while larger siloxanes handle more porous surfaces near the face. A brick wall mixes units and mortar that absorb at different rates, so a blend that covers both is a natural fit. Once it reacts, rain beads and runs off, yet water vapor still passes through, so moisture already inside the wall can dry out. In freeze-thaw country, that breathability matters more than any other property. The wall keeps its natural look, with no gloss and no darkening. Coverage on the data sheet shifts with porosity, so treat a measured section first to learn how thirsty your brick is before buying for the whole house.

**Pros:** silane-siloxane blend for brick, block and concrete; vapor permeable; no change in look; rated for walls and flat surfaces; concentrated.

**Cons:** pricier than big-box masonry sealers; needs 24 to 48 hours of dry weather around application.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ghostshield+Siloxa-Tek+8500&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Value: Masonry Defender Brick Sealer

Masonry Defender is a water-based penetrating sealer for brick, block, stucco and stone. Its silane-siloxane chemistry rides in water, so it goes on easily with a pump sprayer and is much more pleasant to use than a solvent product near windows and doors. Like the better breathable repellents, it leaves the surface looking unchanged and lets the wall release vapor. Its case is value on big jobs. A whole brick house can take many gallons, and the gap between a premium brand and this one grows with every gallon. Very porous antique brick soaks up far more than the best coverage figure on the label, so buy enough for a full saturating coat. As most silane-siloxane labels advise, wet the wall until it just starts to run, then let it dry. It is a smaller brand with less shelf presence, so plan to order it rather than pick it up locally.

**Pros:** breathable; low-odor water carrier; matte, natural look; good price for large areas.

**Cons:** less retail availability; coverage drops sharply on very porous old brick.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Masonry+Defender+Brick+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Water-Based: Foundation Armor SX5000 WB

SX5000 WB is the water-based silane-siloxane in Foundation Armor's long line of masonry sealers. It is rated for brick, concrete, pavers and block, and it aims at the same goals as the premium blends: stop water soaking in, keep vapor moving and leave no visible coating. Low odor and soap-and-water cleanup make it easy to use next to porches and living spaces, and the maker positions it for vertical and horizontal surfaces alike, so a brick patio is as good a target as a wall. Soft, old or very absorbent brick usually does better with a second coat applied wet on wet, before the first has dried. Do not apply it with rain forecast inside the window on the label, which is typically about a day. If you are already using SX5000 on pavers or a concrete walk, one product can cover the whole property.

**Pros:** water-based silane-siloxane; low odor; breathable after cure; rated for brick, pavers, concrete and block.

**Cons:** must stay dry through its cure window; soft brick may need two coats.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Foundation+Armor+SX5000+WB&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Enhanced Look: Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8510

Siloxa-Tek 8510 is the color-enhancing sibling of the 8500. It carries the same penetrating silane-siloxane repellent plus an enhancer that darkens the surface slightly, so the brick looks as if a shower just passed. That suits patios, steps and garden walls bleached by years of sun. Because it soaks in rather than building a film, it does not turn slippery or peel the way acrylic wet-look sealers can on brick pavers, and the brick stays vapor permeable. The deeper color is essentially permanent, so try it on a hidden brick or a spare paver and judge it fully dry before doing the whole area. Dark red or glazed brick often shows very little change, so the effect is most striking on lighter, faded clay. For a brick patio that looks chalky and tired, it is the closest thing to a wet look that stays safe underfoot and breathable in winter.

**Pros:** richer, damp-look color; still breathable; same base as 8500; good for faded patio brick.

**Cons:** permanent darkening, so test first; subtle on dark or glazed brick.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Ghostshield+Siloxa-Tek+8510&tag=sktiger-20)

### Most Accessible: Thompson's WaterSeal Multi-Surface Waterproofer

Thompson's is the name most homeowners already know, and its clear multi-surface waterproofer is labeled for brick and concrete as well as wood. Convenience is the draw: nearly every hardware and home store stocks it, a brush, roller or garden sprayer puts it on, and it costs less than the specialist masonry sealers here. For a brick planter, garden edging or a short wall, that convenience is worth having. Its limits show on bigger, more exposed brickwork. A product built to work on wood too is not tuned for deep penetration into dense masonry, and owners commonly report reapplying it more often than a silane-siloxane. For a whole house, a chimney or a retaining wall, a dedicated masonry repellent lasts longer and protects better. Use it where the job is small and the brick is not taking the full weather.

**Pros:** sold almost everywhere; works on brick, concrete and wood; inexpensive; easy to apply.

**Cons:** shorter service life than masonry repellents; shallower penetration on dense brick.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Thompson%27s+WaterSeal+Multi-Surface+Waterproofer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best for Chimneys: DRYLOK Natural Look Masonry Sealer

DRYLOK is known for basement waterproofing paint, but its Natural Look sealer is a different product: a clear, breathable siloxane repellent for above-grade brick, block and stone. Siloxanes perform well on the moderately porous brick found on many houses and chimneys, and this one dries with no sheen and no darkening. That combination is what a chimney needs, because it takes rain from every side and must also let out moisture coming from inside the structure. Home centers carry it widely, which makes it the practical answer when a chimney needs treating before a wet season and a specialty order would take too long. Flood it onto clean, dry brick with a brush, roller or low-pressure sprayer. It does not reach as deep into very dense brick as silane-rich blends, so on hard-fired face brick the Ghostshield products are the stronger choice.

**Pros:** breathable siloxane; no change in appearance; good on chimneys, walls and foundations above grade; widely available.

**Cons:** less depth than silane blends on dense brick; needs dry weather before and after.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=DRYLOK+Natural+Look+Masonry+Sealer&tag=sktiger-20)

### Best Film-Forming (Interior Brick): Seal-Krete Clear-Seal

Clear-Seal is a water-based acrylic that builds a film on top of the brick rather than soaking in. It adds a satin or gloss finish, deepens the color and locks down loose dust, which is why people use it on interior brick walls, exposed loft brick and the face of a fireplace surround well away from the firebox. Moisture is low indoors, so breathability matters less there. Outdoors, especially on walls in freeze-thaw climates, a film can hold in moisture that enters from behind or through the top of the wall, and spalling and peeling follow. That is why it ranks last for exterior use, even though it does its own job well. Film-formers can also turn slick on wet patios. For an indoor sheen, apply thin coats, work the sealer into the mortar joints and let each coat dry fully before the next.

**Pros:** adds sheen and deepens color; controls dust on interior brick; easy roller application; inexpensive.

**Cons:** not breathable enough for exterior walls; wears and needs recoating; slippery on wet pavers.

[Check price on Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/s?k=Seal-Krete+Clear-Seal&tag=sktiger-20)

sections.heading: Should You Seal Brick at All?
sections.body:
### Find the real water source first

Good face brick is fired clay and holds up well on its own. The weak points in most walls are the mortar joints, flashing, caps and gutters. If a wall is getting wet, look for spilling gutters, missing drip edges, failed caulk around windows or worn-out mortar first. Sealing a wall with any of those faults treats the symptom and leaves the cause.

### Signs brick needs a sealer

Brick that stays dark for hours after rain, white efflorescence salts, spalling faces, damp patches on the inside of solid masonry walls and moss or algae on shaded faces all point to brick soaking up too much water. Soft historic brick, sand-molded brick and walls in heavy weather are the usual candidates.

### The hose test

Spray a section of wall for a minute and watch. If water runs off and the brick returns to its dry color within a few minutes, absorption is modest and sealing is optional. If the brick drinks it in and stays dark for an hour, it is taking on more moisture than is healthy. Test more than one wall; the side facing the prevailing weather often behaves very differently from a sheltered side.

### Check the mortar

Joints recessed by more than about a quarter inch, or mortar that crumbles when scraped with a key, need repointing first. Sealer will not hold in failing mortar, and repointing is the repair that actually stops water at the joints.

sections.heading: Why Does Exterior Brick Sealer Need to Be Breathable?
sections.body:
### Trapped water and freeze-thaw

Water in the outer layer of brick expands by roughly 9 percent as it freezes. Winter after winter, that pressure breaks away the face of the brick, the failure called spalling. A glossy acrylic or heavy paint on exterior brick can collect moisture right behind the film and make spalling worse.

### How penetrating repellents work

Silane and siloxane repellents line the pores with a water-shedding layer without plugging them. Liquid water beads and runs away while vapor keeps moving outward. That is why masonry restoration guidance, including the Brick Industry Association's, favors breathable clear repellents over films when a treatment is needed at all.

### Silane, siloxane or a blend?

Silanes reach deepest into dense material, siloxanes do well on more porous surfaces, and blends cover both. Since brick and mortar absorb at different rates, blends are a strong default for walls.

| Sealer type | Breathable | Look | Typical life | Use on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Silane-siloxane penetrating | Yes | Natural | 5 to 10 years, by label claims | Walls, chimneys, retaining walls |
| Siloxane penetrating | Yes | Natural | Several years | Moderately porous brick |
| Enhancing penetrating | Yes | Darker, wet look | Several years | Patios, garden walls |
| Acrylic film | Limited | Satin to gloss | 1 to 3 years | Interior or covered brick |
| Masonry paint | Varies | Opaque | Varies | Only breathable masonry formulas |

### Judging a brand not on this list

Shoppers often ask about other masonry sealers, such as A-Tech or Center Stage brick sealers. Judge any of them the same way: does the label call it penetrating and vapor permeable, does it name brick as an approved surface, and is it rated for vertical, above-grade exterior use? If the label says film, gloss or coating, keep it indoors.

sections.heading: What Is the Best Sealer for Brick Walls, Chimneys, Patios and Interior Brick?
sections.body:
### Exterior walls

Use a breathable silane-siloxane rated for vertical above-grade masonry: Siloxa-Tek 8500, Masonry Defender or SX5000 WB. Check that the data sheet describes it as vapor permeable.

### Chimneys

The same type, with breathability weighted even more heavily, since a chimney takes rain from every side and releases moisture from within. DRYLOK Natural Look and both Ghostshield products suit chimney brick. A repellent does not fix a cracked crown or failed flashing, so repair those first.

### Brick patios, walkways and steps

Use a penetrating repellent rated for horizontal surfaces; it reduces freeze damage and leaves traction unchanged. For richer color, Siloxa-Tek 8510. Skip high-gloss films, which get slick when wet and wear in patchy lanes. Brick pavers set in sand also need their joints stabilized, which our [paver sealer guide](/best-paver-sealer/) covers, and our [water-based paver sealer roundup](/best-water-based-paver-sealer-reviews/) lists low-odor options.

### Retaining and garden walls

Drainage first: gravel backfill, a perforated drain at the base and weep holes. Then treat the exposed face only with a breathable repellent; never coat the face to try to waterproof the wall from the front. On garden walls, a sound cap with a drip edge does most of the work, and the cap and top courses deserve the most sealer.

### Interior brick and fireplace surrounds

A film-former such as Seal-Krete Clear-Seal is fine indoors, where it controls dust and adds sheen. Keep every sealer out of the firebox.

### Foundations and basement walls

Clear above-grade repellents are not built for below-grade water pressure. For leaking basement walls see our [basement wall sealer guide](/best-basement-wall-sealer/), and for block rather than brick, our [cinder block paint guide](/best-paint-for-cinder-block/).

sections.heading: Will Brick Sealer Stop Efflorescence, Spalling or Moss?
sections.body:
### Efflorescence

Efflorescence is the white powder left when water carries salts to the surface and evaporates. A sealer can reduce new efflorescence by limiting how much water enters the wall, but it does not remove existing deposits, and sealing over active salts can push crystallization just beneath the surface, where it does more harm. Dry-brush the deposits, use a masonry cleaner made for efflorescence on stubborn salts, rinse and wait until the wall stays clean through a few dry weeks.

### Spalling

Do not seal spalled brick; replace it. Once the hard face is gone, the softer inner body absorbs even more water. Replace the damaged units, fix the water source, then protect the rest of the wall.

### Moss and algae

These grow on brick that stays damp, usually on north-facing or shaded walls. Remove them with a biocidal masonry cleaner and a soft brush, not a high-pressure wash. A repellent applied afterward helps the wall dry faster, so regrowth comes back more slowly.

### Historic and soft brick

Old, soft brick and lime mortar depend on breathing more than modern brick. Many preservation specialists advise against sealing historic masonry unless repairs alone cannot solve a specific water problem. If you must, use only a highly breathable penetrant and test it first.

sections.heading: How Do You Prep and Apply Brick Sealer?
sections.body:
### Clean, repair, dry

Match the cleaner to the soil: biocidal for algae, efflorescence cleaner for salts, masonry detergent for dirt. Scrub with a stiff natural or nylon brush, never a wire brush on soft brick. If you pressure wash, keep the pressure modest and use a wide fan tip held a foot or more away; high pressure erodes mortar and strips the fired skin off soft brick. Repoint eroded joints, replace spalled units and caulk gaps around windows and penetrations. Fresh mortar needs to cure, often for weeks, before sealing.

### Conditions

Most silane-siloxane labels want brick dry to the touch, at least 24 hours after rain or washing, and mild temperatures, often around 40 to 90 degrees Fahrenheit. Cover plants, windows and trim with plastic first.

### Apply from the bottom up

Use a low-pressure pump sprayer and work from the bottom of the wall up. Flood the surface until sealer runs down 6 to 8 inches below the spray pattern; that rundown tells you the brick is saturated. Back-brush puddles on ledges. Work from one natural break, such as a corner or downspout, to the next to avoid lap marks.

### Second coat and weather

Many products call for a second coat wet on wet, before the first dries. Once the first coat reacts, the surface repels the second, so follow the label timing. Avoid hot direct sun and any rain inside the label window, often 12 to 24 hours. Repellency builds over a few days, so do not judge it by hosing the wall the next morning.

### Safety

Wear the gloves and eye protection the label calls for, add a respirator for solvent products and wipe overspray off glass right away with the solvent the label names.

sections.heading: How Much Brick Sealer Do You Need, and What Does It Cost?
sections.body:
### Coverage depends on porosity

Dense, hard-fired face brick may spread a gallon over 150 to 250 square feet. Soft or sand-molded brick may take a gallon every 75 to 125 square feet. Seal a measured section first, work out what you actually used and only then buy for the whole house.

### Measuring

Multiply length by height for each wall and subtract large openings such as garage doors. A typical two-story brick house can carry 2,000 square feet or more of brick, which means 10 to 20 gallons or more for one coat on porous brick. A chimney might be 100 to 200 square feet; a patio is simply its floor area.

### Price tiers

Big-box multi-surface products sit at the low end per gallon, mid-range masonry repellents in the middle and concentrated premium silane-siloxanes at the top. Premium products often cover more area per gallon, which narrows the gap.

### Hiring it out

Contractors commonly quote about $1 to $3 per square foot, more when cleaning, repointing or work at height is included. A single-story wall reachable from a ladder is a manageable DIY job. Two-story walls, chimneys and steep roofs are where a crew with staging and fall protection is worth paying.

sections.heading: What Is the Longest Lasting Brick Sealer?
sections.body:
### Penetrating repellents last longest

On walls, silane-siloxane repellents commonly carry life claims of 5 to 10 years, and some premium products claim more. Horizontal surfaces such as patios and wall caps wear faster from foot traffic, standing water and sun, and often need attention every 3 to 5 years. Films typically need recoating every 1 to 3 years.

### Why films cost more over time

A worn film looks patchy and may peel, and recoating over a degraded film gives uneven results. The old layer often has to come off with a chemical stripper first, which is slow, messy work on textured brick. A penetrant never needs stripping; clean the wall and apply another coat the same way.

### When to reseal

Repeat the hose test every year or two. When water stops beading and the brick darkens fast and stays dark, the repellent is fading.

### Making each coat last

Keep gutters clean, maintain caulk at windows and penetrations, and repoint as soon as joints start to erode. Those details keep more water out of the wall than any sealer, and every coat of repellent lasts longer because of them. On patios, sweep off leaves and planters that hold moisture against the brick.

mistakes.title: Putting a glossy film on exterior brick
mistakes.body: Acrylic and polyurethane films look great on day one, then hold moisture inside exterior brick, worst where winters freeze and thaw. Within a few winters that can mean peeling, cloudy patches and spalled faces. Use a breathable penetrant outdoors and keep films for interior brick.

mistakes.title: Sealing over efflorescence
mistakes.body: White salt deposits mean the wall is moving water. Seal over them and the salts can crystallize just beneath the surface and break off the brick face. Clean the deposits, fix the moisture source and wait until the wall stays clean through a dry spell before sealing.

mistakes.title: Skipping mortar repairs
mistakes.body: Most water enters a wall through the mortar, not the brick, and no sealer fills eroded or cracked joints. Repoint failing joints first and give fresh mortar the full cure time its maker specifies. Sealing over open joints wastes product and leaves every leak path in place.

mistakes.title: Applying too little product
mistakes.body: A penetrating repellent protects by depth. A light misting looks finished but treats only a shallow layer that wears away quickly. Flood the brick until sealer runs several inches below the spray, and add a wet-on-wet second coat when the label calls for one.

mistakes.title: Blasting brick with high pressure
mistakes.body: An aggressive pressure wash wears down mortar and strips the fired skin off softer brick, leaving a rougher, thirstier surface than before. Clean with a masonry cleaner and stiff brush, keep any pressure low and the tip well back, and let the wall dry fully before sealing.

faqs.q: What is the best brick sealer for exterior walls?
faqs.a: Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500 is the best brick sealer for most exterior walls and chimneys. It is a breathable silane-siloxane repellent that sheds rain while letting moisture inside the wall escape, and it leaves the brick looking unchanged. Masonry Defender and Foundation Armor SX5000 WB are lower-cost water-based alternatives that work the same way.

faqs.q: What is the top rated brick patio sealer?
faqs.a: For a brick patio, a penetrating repellent rated for horizontal surfaces is the safest choice, and Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8510 is the pick if you want richer color. It darkens faded brick slightly without a slippery film. If the brick is set in sand, stabilize the joints too, ideally with polymeric sand, before sealing.

faqs.q: What is the longest lasting brick sealer?
faqs.a: Penetrating silane-siloxane repellents last longest. On walls they commonly carry maker life claims of 5 to 10 years between coats, with patios and wall caps due sooner. Film-forming sealers often need recoating every one to three years and may need stripping first. Good gutters, flashing and mortar make any sealer last longer.

faqs.q: Does brick sealer darken or add shine to brick?
faqs.a: A standard penetrating repellent leaves brick looking unchanged once dry, although the wall can look darker for a few hours while wet. Enhancing products such as Siloxa-Tek 8510 darken it on purpose, and acrylic films add sheen and deepen color. Try any product on a hidden spot and judge it fully dry first.

faqs.q: Can I use concrete sealer on brick?
faqs.a: It depends on the type. Penetrating silane-siloxane sealers are often labeled for concrete, brick, block and pavers, and those suit brick. Film-forming concrete sealers such as high-gloss driveway acrylics limit breathability and are a poor match for exterior brick walls. Confirm the label names brick and says vapor permeable.

faqs.q: Will a brick sealer stop efflorescence?
faqs.a: Not on its own. A repellent can cut future efflorescence by limiting how much water enters the brick, but it leaves existing deposits and cannot stop salts driven by water from behind or below. Clean the deposits, repair gutters, grading and flashing, and seal only once the wall stays dry.

faqs.q: Should old or historic brick be sealed?
faqs.a: Only with care. Soft brick and lime mortar depend on breathing more than modern brick, so if sealing is truly needed, use only a highly breathable penetrating repellent and test it first. Many preservation specialists advise against sealing historic masonry unless repairs alone cannot fix a specific water problem.

bottomLine: For exterior brick walls and chimneys, Ghostshield Siloxa-Tek 8500 is the best all-around sealer, with Masonry Defender and Foundation Armor SX5000 WB as cheaper water-based alternatives that do the same breathable job. Siloxa-Tek 8510 is the pick for faded brick patios, DRYLOK Natural Look is the convenient home-center chimney option, Thompson's covers small projects, and Seal-Krete Clear-Seal belongs indoors. Sort out gutters, flashing and mortar first, then decide whether the brick still needs help, and when it does, choose breathability over shine every time.
